- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underestimating downside.  
- If recent history shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast 10–15% in next period.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true values by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 2–3% from next forecast.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low) and forecast is erratic, use 3-day moving average of true values as anchor for next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of historical mean, adjust forecast downward by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion bias.
